solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Order to Harlequins' backs, maybe: 'Help with lifting!'

definitions.meaning: Harlequins are a London rugby union club; a coach might shout to the backs to block opponents and then bring them down
a pulley system with rope used to hoist heavy loads

explanation.surface: A rugby coach yells at his team's back line, but it sounds like a cry for help with heavy lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins are an English rugby union club; 'backs' are the players behind the scrum, whose defensive job is to block and tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulley arrangement of ropes and sheaves is the classic mechanical aid for hoisting heavy weights.

clue.text: One can gain entry to remarkable bloke's monument

indicators.note: getting in means this piece goes inside the shuffled letters
something remarkable is out of the ordinary, so the letters of the word bloke's are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A single visitor can get into some notable man's memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges BLOKES to OBELKS, and 'can gain entry to' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering stone pillar is a classic kind of commemorative monument, like Cleopatra's Needle.

clue.text: Joint where Kate's first's born …

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Kate's is taken

parts.note: née, from French, marks a woman's maiden name: born as

explanation.surface: A question of where Kate's first child was born, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue's surface to the next one; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge between thigh and shin is a body joint.

clue.text: … in its early weeks showing something noble towards nearly everyone

parts.note: neon is one of the noble gases
at, as in aiming at something, means towards

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a newborn in its first weeks shows noble qualities towards almost everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ALL to AL. Neon is a noble gas, a chemistry convention that hides behind the sense of nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal describes a baby in its first month of life, the earliest weeks after birth.

clue.text: Hip operation on Ned ends in outright disaster; misery all round

indicators.note: these letters go all round the shuffled piece
the final letters of the three words outright, disaster and misery are taken
an operation on something works it over, so the letters of Ned are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ned's hip operation ends in total disaster and misery for everyone around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' looks like the body part being operated on, but it is the slang definition; 'operation on' is the anagram signal, 'ends in' picks final letters and 'all round' wraps them round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip in its slang sense means fashionable, up to date with the latest styles.

clue.text: With energy control not working — raised in Cabinet

parts.note: chi (qi) is life energy in Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means these letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rein in is to control
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: A government minister, energetic but out of control, is promoted into the Cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' with its capital suggests government, but it is furniture. Chi (qi) is the life force of Chinese thought; 'raised' reverses only the control and not-working pieces, upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiffonier is a piece of furniture: a low sideboard or tall chest of drawers, so a type of cabinet.

clue.text: Heartless devil deserts suckers in lounges

indicators.note: to desert something is to leave it, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: lollipops are sweets on sticks that are sucked

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A cruel demon abandons the sweets lying around in the lounges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' cuts IMP to IP, and 'deserts' takes IP out of LOLLIPOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to lounge or loll about in a relaxed, ungainly way.

clue.text: Surprisingly worn pipes to outlets

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters come out in an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: Old, worn pipes are unexpectedly connected to drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges the eleven letters of WORN PIPES TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall sockets supplying mains electricity are electrical outlets.

clue.text: Faithful wife given pound tip to embrace pole dancing

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: pene, a variant of peen, is the tip of a hammer head used for pounding

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the letters of pole are rearranged

explanation.surface: A devoted wife is paid a pound as a tip to take up pole dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests money, but the pound tip is the pene (peen, pein), the striking end of a hammer head. 'dancing' rearranges the pole and 'to embrace' wraps the hammer end round it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey, Odysseus's wife waits twenty years for him, refusing every suitor: the model of marital loyalty.

clue.text: Back in cool gite? Cool, yes, but different lodgings!

indicators.note: back means the letters are read from right to left
in shows the letters sit inside the words cool gite

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a French holiday cottage cool, though not the kind of cool he meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks OOLGI out of 'cOOL GIte' and 'Back' reverses it. A gîte is a French holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome of snow blocks is a dwelling that is literally cold, a very different place to stay.

clue.text: Beaks tut too about laws in general

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Magistrates tut disapprovingly over the laws in general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BEAKS TUT TOO. Beak is British slang for a magistrate, which suits the legal surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of legislation in force is collectively called the statute book.

clue.text: Musketeers perhaps enjoying spot of tawny port

indicators.note: a spot is a small amount, so just the first letter of the word tawny

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: The Musketeers enjoy a drop of tawny port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, but it is a harbour city: RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumas's Three Musketeers, Athos, Porthos and Aramis, are a group of three.

clue.text: Young abstainers given cynic's wedding-ring?

definitions.meaning: a Victorian temperance society for children who pledged not to drink
a cynic would see a wedding ring as a ring of mere optimism

explanation.surface: Teetotal youngsters are handed a cynic's view of a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Band of Hope was a British temperance movement for working-class children, founded in 1847.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a ring worn at a wedding is a circlet of optimism, which is how a cynic would see marriage.

clue.text: Bottle extraordinary soup –- it's a chef d'oeuvre!

parts.note: a magnum is a large wine bottle, twice the standard size

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters of soup are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook bottles an exceptional soup and declares it a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges SOUP to OPUS. 'chef' looks like a cook but is French for chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Chef d'oeuvre is French for masterpiece, and the Latin phrase means an artist's greatest work.

clue.text: It's to go — remove!

definitions.meaning: food bought to be eaten elsewhere, ordered to go
to remove something is to carry it off

explanation.surface: Something has to go, so get rid of it.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the noun, a meal ordered to go; the other is the verb phrase, to take something off.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal bought from a shop to eat elsewhere is the noun sense; carrying something off is the verb sense.

clue.text: Arrives with intent to imbibe

parts.note: an end is an aim or intent
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone shows up with every intention of drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish up somewhere is to arrive there eventually, often unplanned.

clue.text: Hood's lady-friend cuddling Charlie — old boxer

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hug, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: Maid Marian is Robin Hood's sweetheart
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's sweetheart hugs a man called Charlie, an old fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuddling' puts C inside MARIAN, then O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky Marciano was the American heavyweight champion of the 1950s who retired unbeaten.

clue.text: Eating out, it's on the menu

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: When you eat out, this is what the menu offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EATING. 'Eating out' reads as dining in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African slow-cooked stew, named after its conical pot, is a dish found on restaurant menus.

clue.text: An interruption like this is in the air

definitions.text: An interruption like this is in the air

parts.words: An interruption like this is in the air
parts.note: a stop made by closing the vocal folds briefly halts the flow of air through the throat

explanation.surface: Something like an interruption hangs in the air, as a rumour might.
explanation.walkthrough: The stop referred to is the catch in the throat that replaces the t in a Cockney 'bu'er'; it interrupts the breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The glottis is the opening between the vocal cords, and closing it cuts off the airstream for an instant.

clue.text: Skimming device made from wet hide, mostly

parts.note: to water something is to wet it

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an animal's skin is its hide

explanation.surface: A device for skimming made mostly from wet leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SKIN to SKI. 'Skimming' suggests cream or stones, but it is gliding over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A board towed behind a motorboat lets a rider skim over the surface of the lake.

clue.text: Trim last of shrubs on bank?

indicators.note: the last letter of the word shrubs is taken

parts.note: a bank is a lender of money

explanation.surface: A gardener is asked to trim the last of the shrubs growing on a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests a riverside, but it is a moneylender. 'on' here just joins, and in a down clue S sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means slim and lean, as a fit figure is.

clue.text: Attack from fliers in mostly worrying situation

indicators.note: in shows the airmen are placed inside the shortened word
mostly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be in a state of worry
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's military fliers

explanation.surface: Pilots carry out an attack in a mostly anxious situation.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'in a stew' is to be in a fluster; 'mostly' trims that word and 'in' places the Royal Air Force within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Potter's implement (British) given space alongside spear

indicators.note: alongside means the next piece goes beside the previous ones

parts.note: room means space
to stick is to spear or pierce

explanation.surface: A potter's tool, British-made, sits next to space and a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests a ceramicist, but it is Harry Potter, who flies on one.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter flies a witch's sweeping brush in Quidditch matches, so it is his signature piece of kit.

clue.text: Live on street that's most desirable

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Living on a particular street is the most desirable option.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of good describes whatever is most wanted or finest.

clue.text: Blarney Stone's summit –- senior citizen's below

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts this piece under the first letter
the summit is the top, so the first letter of Stone's

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An elderly person stands below the top of the Blarney Stone in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blarney Stone, kissed for the gift of the gab, makes 'Blarney Stone' look like one phrase, but 'Blarney' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is flattery, and blarney is smooth, flattering talk.

clue.text: Where 'H' and 'C' are seen to be available?

definitions.meaning: the letters for hot and cold appear on bathroom fittings

explanation.surface: A question about where hot and cold markings appear in a bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer served from a barrel is said to be readily available, ready to draw at any moment.

clue.text: It's said Karenin's wife handled a serpent

indicators.note: it's said means the words are spoken and the sound is what counts

parts.note: Anna is Karenin's wife in Tolstoy's novel, and conned means handled, as a ship is steered, then a

explanation.surface: Tolstoy's heroine is rumoured to have handled a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: To con a ship is to steer it, so conned means handled. The phrase spoken, ANNA CONNED A, gives the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant South American constrictor is one of the largest snakes.

clue.text: Cast's material could make opera stars flip insanely

indicators.note: insanely means wildly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The cast of an opera could drive its stars crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insanely' rearranges OPERA STARS FLIP. 'Cast' suggests a theatre company, but it is a plaster for a broken limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum powder mixed with water sets hard and is used for casts on broken bones.
